The attack: attacker directly sends JSON-RPC tools/call register_tool. No authentication. Tool registration changes advertised registry in-process; registered tools get no new handler (per agent-success-paths comments) — so impact is modification of the tool list (integrity low), shadowing built-in tools, up to 16 entries. Registered tool executes nothing new (no handler). So VI L on vulnerable system (registry poisoning). VC N (no data exposure... registration reply echoes registryUrl but no secrets). Availability: registry full refusal possible — minor; VA L? Filling 16 slots refuses new registrations — that's low availability? It's a limited resource exhaustion: registering 16 tools blocks future registrations. Could rate VA L. Subsequent systems: none — in-process. SC/SI/SA N.

AV: Network (MCP port, loopback-published by default but Docker; entry point precondition network access to port). Score as documented default deployment: Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1; attacker needs network access to the port — same machine or lab network. AV N (network reachable), UI N, PR N, AC L, AT N.

AIVSS: LC — attacker-supplied natural language (tool name/description) reaches a privileged tool path without mediation → D? The arguments name/description are attacker language entering the tool registry directly. It's an MCP call, not really NL to LLM. But LC is about natural-language path to security-relevant behavior; here attacker-controlled fields directly registered. It's Direct (D): attacker-supplied language reaches a privileged tool-invocation path without mediation. I'd say D.

CP: registration persists in-process (in-memory dynamicTools/agent.tools) beyond the request — persists across sessions until restart? It's in-memory server state, persists across requests/sessions of the server process. Not durable store though. "Session context" is ephemeral per session; this is process-lifetime state, reachable after originating session ends → C? CP C requires durable stores (vector DBs, memory). In-memory registry persists across sessions but not durable. Rubric S: "ephemeral session state... testing confirms unreachable after session boundary." Here state persists after session ends, but not durable. I'd pick C given it persists and remains reachable across sessions? C's definition lists durable stores. In-process registry isn't listed but "remains reachable after originating session ends" — no test confirms otherwise. Hmm. I'll say S? No—S requires confirmed unreachable. Registry persists in server process. I'll pick C with medium/low confidence. Actually CP X also defensible. I'll pick C.

AP: Contained (in-process components, same agent). PluginBot only; other agents could call its tools via fetch_url loopback? Propagation confined to PluginBot's own registry — N? Effect confined to initially affected component (PluginBot). AP N.

RH: proxy/evaluator on path? No evaluator. reachable_proxy null → X. verified_episodes null.

ES: Wide (W) — dynamic tool registration with no signature/schema check.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Technical impact: Partial (registry modification, no code execution since no handler bound). Automatable: Yes (curl, no human).

Applicability: default simulated mode, no LLM tools passed to model — agent doesn't pursue goals/selects actions? PluginBot is an MCP tool server, scripted. model_directed_goal_pursuit false, selects_or_sequences_actions false, both as-implemented and as-modeled (documentation describes scripted simulated tool server).

CVSS rationale: unauthenticated network caller modifies PluginBot's tool registry; impact limited to tool list integrity (no handler executes attacker code); attacker already "owns" nothing on the asset but no auth needed.

AV: default binds 127.0.0.1 — attacker needs local presence? Briefing says precondition network access to MCP port. Docker sets 0.0.0.0 inside but published on 127.0.0.1. Given documented deployment reachable via localhost from same machine — could be AV:L? Entry point is a network request; agents on loopback, so attacker on same machine (or lab network when exposed). FIRST: loopback-only = local. I'd say AV:L given default 127.0.0.1 binding... but Docker container binds 0.0.0.0 and port published to 127.0.0.1 — still local-only access from host. Network from other containers? Adjacent. Hmm. Default documented: published ports on 127.0.0.1 → attacker must be on same machine → AV:L. I'll go AV:L with medium confidence, mention exposure option in rationale. Actually the challenge intends network exploit; but scoring "as documented default deployment" — loopback. AV:L.
